In [[mathematics]], an '''orthogonal symmetric Lie algebra''' is a pair <math>(\mathfrak{g}, s)</math> consisting of a real [[Lie algebra]] <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> and an [[automorphism]] <math>s</math> of <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> of order <math>2</math> such that the [[eigenspace]] <math>\mathfrak{u}</math> of ''s'' corresponding to 1 (i.e., the set <math>\mathfrak{u}</math> of [[Fixed point (mathematics)|fixed points]]) is a [[compact Lie algebra|compact subalgebra]]. If "compactness" is omitted, it is called a '''symmetric Lie algebra'''. An orthogonal symmetric Lie algebra is said to be ''effective'' if <math>\mathfrak{u}</math> intersects the [[Center (group theory)|center]] of <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> [[trivial group|trivially]]. In practice, effectiveness is often assumed; we do this in this article as well.

The canonical example is the Lie algebra of a [[symmetric space]], <math>s</math> being the differential of a symmetry.

Let <math>(\mathfrak{g}, s)</math> be effective orthogonal symmetric Lie algebra, and let <math>\mathfrak{p}</math>  denotes the -1 eigenspace of <math>s</math>. We say that <math>(\mathfrak{g}, s)</math> is ''of compact type'' if <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> is [[Compact Lie algebra|compact]] and [[Semisimple Lie algebra|semisimple]]. If instead it is noncompact, semisimple, and if <math>\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{u}+\mathfrak{p}</math> is a Cartan decomposition, then <math>(\mathfrak{g}, s)</math> is ''of noncompact type''. If <math>\mathfrak{p}</math> is an Abelian ideal of <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>, then <math>(\mathfrak{g}, s)</math> is said to be ''of Euclidean type''.

Every effective, orthogonal symmetric Lie algebra decomposes into a [[direct sum]] of ideals <math>\mathfrak{g}_0</math>, <math>\mathfrak{g}_-</math> and <math>\mathfrak{g}_+</math>, each invariant under <math>s</math> and orthogonal with respect to the [[Killing form]] of <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>, and such that if <math>s_0</math>, <math>s_-</math> and <math>s_+</math> denote the restriction of <math>s</math> to <math>\mathfrak{g}_0</math>, <math>\mathfrak{g}_-</math> and <math>\mathfrak{g}_+</math>, respectively, then <math>(\mathfrak{g}_0,s_0)</math>, <math>(\mathfrak{g}_-,s_-)</math> and <math>(\mathfrak{g}_+,s_+)</math> are effective orthogonal symmetric Lie algebras of Euclidean type, compact type and noncompact type.
